title: Police Blotter: 13 booked in Webb County — end-of-day roundup
excerpt: Thirteen people were booked into the Webb County Jail on November 16, 2026, on alleged misdemeanor charges and holds — DWI, assault, theft, resisting arrest and more. Every arrest is an allegation; each person is presumed innocent until proven guilty.
content:
Thirteen people were booked into the Webb County Jail on Monday, November 16, 2026, on alleged misdemeanor charges and holds, according to Webb County booking records. Each person is listed below with the charge shown in their booking record. An arrest is an allegation, not a conviction, and every person named here is presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

Jose Manuel Martinez

Jose Manuel Martinez was arrested on Monday, November 16, 2026, at 2:14 a.m. on an alleged charge of assault causing bodily injury — family member, a Class A misdemeanor. Bond was set at $5,000. He was arrested by the Laredo Police Department.

Leonardo De Leon

Leonardo De Leon was arrested on Monday, November 16, 2026, at 5:04 a.m. on an alleged charge of assault causing bodily injury — family member, a Class A misdemeanor. Bond was set at $5,000. He was arrested by the Webb County Sheriff's Office.

Fiorella Chapa

Fiorella Chapa was arrested on Monday, November 16, 2026, at 7:02 a.m. on an alleged charge of driving while intoxicated with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.15 or higher, a Class A misdemeanor. Bond was set at $3,000. She was magistrated on Monday, November 16, 2026, at 2:54 p.m. The arresting agency was not listed in the booking record.

Adrian Ramiro Rocha

Adrian Ramiro Rocha was arrested on Monday, November 16, 2026, at 7:24 a.m. on alleged charges of fraud — destroying, removing or concealing a writing, a Class A misdemeanor; evading arrest or detention, a Class A misdemeanor; resisting arrest, search or transport, a Class A misdemeanor; a second count of evading arrest or detention, a Class A misdemeanor; a second count of resisting arrest, search or transport, a Class A misdemeanor; driving while intoxicated, a Class B misdemeanor; and driving with an invalid license with a previous conviction, suspension or without financial responsibility, a Class B misdemeanor. Bond had not been set on the first three charges at the time of booking. Bond was set at $3,000 on the second evading arrest charge, $2,000 on the second resisting arrest charge, $2,000 on the driving while intoxicated charge and $1,000 on the driving with an invalid license charge. He was arrested by the Laredo Police Department.

Ricardo Ramirez Jr.

Ricardo Ramirez Jr. was arrested on Monday, November 16, 2026, at 8:17 a.m. on an alleged charge of driving while intoxicated with an open alcohol container, a Class B misdemeanor. No bond had been set at the time of booking. The arresting agency was not listed in the booking record.
